questions.question: Which detergents are also used in toothpaste?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anionic detergents**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Anionic detergents are commonly used in **toothpaste due to their effective cleansing properties.**
 
• **Sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS)** is a prevalent anionic detergent found in many toothpaste formulations.
 
• Anionic detergents help in creating foam, which aids in the mechanical removal of food particles and plaque.
 
• These detergents are also responsible for the dispersion of ingredients in toothpaste, ensuring a uniform mixture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Surfactants:**

 
 
• Surfactants are compounds that lower the surface tension between two substances, such as a solid and a liquid.
 
• They are a key ingredient in many cleaning products, including toothpaste, detergents, and shampoos.
 
• Anionic surfactants, like sodium lauryl sulfate, are particularly effective in removing dirt and oil.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS):**
 
 
• SLS is one of the most commonly used surfactants in toothpaste and other personal care products.
 
• It is known for its ability to produce a rich lather, which helps in the thorough cleaning of teeth.
 
• Despite its effectiveness, SLS can cause irritation in some individuals, leading to the development of alternative formulations.
 
 
 
• **Toothpaste Ingredients:**
 
 
• Common ingredients in toothpaste include abrasives, fluoride, flavoring agents, and humectants.
 
• Abrasives help in removing plaque and stains from the teeth, while fluoride strengthens tooth enamel.
 
• Humectants prevent the toothpaste from drying out, ensuring it remains usable over time.
 
 
 
• **Non-Ionic Detergents:**
 
 
• Non-ionic detergents are another class of surfactants that do not carry any charge.
 
• They are less likely to cause irritation and are often used in products designed for sensitive skin.
 
• While effective in cleaning, they are not as commonly used in toothpaste as anionic detergents.

questions.question: Which of the following is a form of calcium carbonate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Limestone__**.

__
 
• **Limestone **is a form of calcium carbonate.
 
• Other Different forms of calcium carbonate are **Chalk and Marble.**
 
• Calcium carbonate is a chemical compound with the formula **CaCO₃.**
 
• It is a common substance found in rocks as the minerals **calcite and aragonite** (most notably as limestone, which is a type of sedimentary rock consisting mainly of calcite) and is the main component of **eggshells, snail shells, sea shells, and pearls.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Properties of Calcium Carbonate:**

 
• Molar mass - 100.0869 g/mol.
 
• Odor - odorless.
 
• Appearance - Fine white powder; chalky taste.
 
• pH value - 9

questions.question: Which of the following can be beaten into thin sheets?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Malleability:**

 
 
• Malleability is a physical property of** metals that defines their ability to be hammered, pressed, or rolled into thin sheets** without breaking.
 
• In other words, it is the property of a metal to **deform under compression **and take on a new shape.
 
• Metals with close-packed structures such as **copper, gold, silver, zinc, magnesium,** etc. are in general more malleable than those with the loose-packed structure (tungsten, vanadium, chromium, etc.).
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/363725e60cb6bcaae2b408dd50d62e13c2e79341a193df56c68af12fc2192fe2.png] 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• **Phosphorus, Sulphur, and oxygen are non-metals **and hence, cannot be shaped into sheets.

questions.question: Stainless steel is very useful material in our life. In stainless steel, iron is mixed with
questions.solution:
__**Concept **__- 

**Alloys**:

__
 
• Alloys are metal mixtures with additional elements whose **precise composition** is dictated by the qualities required.
 
• They are metallic in nature, which means they have **strong thermal and electrical conductivity**.
 
• Alloys are metal alloys or metal alloys with additional elements.
 
• Other metals/elements can be added to metals in certain ratios to make alloys that give specific properties or strengthen some of the metals' existing properties.
 
• In simple terms, an alloy is a **homogenous **blend of two or more metals, or a metal and a non-metal.
 
• Examples -

 
• **Steel **

 
 
• Steel is a very popular alloy because of its inexpensive cost and great tensile strength.
 
• It is an alloy made up of iron(Fe) and carbon(C).
 
 
 
• **Bronze **
 
 
• Bronze is a copper(Cu) and tin(Sn) alloy.
 
• Medals, coins, trophies, hefty gears and tools, and several types of electrical devices all employ it.
 
 
 
• **Nichrome **
 
 
• Nichrome is an alloy made mostly of nickel(Ni) and chromium(Cr).
 
• Resistance wires are the most common use of nichrome.
 
• Certain electrical equipment, such as space heaters and bread toasters, employ it as the heating element.
 
 
 
• **Brass **
 
 
• Brass is a copper-zinc alloy with variable proportions of copper(Cu) and zinc(Zn) to obtain different mechanical, electrical, and chemical properties.
 
• It's also been commonly utilized for utensils of many kinds.
 
• Because of its dazzling gold-like appearance, brass has long been a desirable decorative material.
 
 
 
• **Stainless Steel** 
 
 
• It is an alloy of **iron(Fe), Nickel(Ni), **and **chromium(Cr). **
 
• Utensils are made from stainless steel.
 
• This alloy does not undergo rusting. 
 
 

**Explanation - **__

 
• Stainless steel does not undergo rusting. 
 
• It is an alloy of - iron(Fe), Nickel (Ni), and Chromium (Cr).
 
• It has a wide range of applications it is used in Buildings, to make utensils, and sometimes jewellery.
 
• Hence, the correct answer to this question is - **Nickel(Ni) and Chromium(Cr)**.
 
 
• It is made up of iron mixed with nickel and chromium.

questions.question: Which of the following metal is kept in wax?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lithium. **__

__**Explanation**__:

 
• **Group I elements are called alkali metals** because they dissolve in water to form soluble hydroxides.
 
• To prevent Group I elements from reacting with water moisture in the air they are kept in kerosene oil.
 
 
• **Example: **Sodium, Potassium.
 
 
 
• But** Lithium is the lightest metal** and it **floats above the kerosene surface** and reacts with atmospheric oxygen or moisture.

So, **Lithium** is kept in wax.

questions.question: Which among the following is an active ingredient in antacids?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium Bicarbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium bicarbonate is an active ingredient of Antacids.**
 
• It is also known as **Sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO3).**
 
• Sodium bicarbonate reduces stomach acid.
 
• It is used as an antacid to treat heartburn, indigestion, and upset stomach.
 
• Sodium bicarbonate is a very quick-acting antacid.
 
• Sodium bicarbonate is a white solid that is crystalline.
 
• It has a slightly salty, alkaline taste.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The common name of **Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO3)** is baking soda.
 
• **Baking soda is pure sodium bicarbonate.**
 
• Baking powder or Sodium Hydrogen Carbonate NaHCO3.
 
• Baking powder is a mixture of several chemical compounds including sodium bicarbonate, an acidifying agent and a drying agent. Both baking powder and baking soda have the same formulae.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sodium Chloride is Common salt.
 
• Sodium Hydroxide is Caustic Soda.
 
• Sodium Carbonate is Washing Soda.

questions.question: Thermodynamically the most stable form of carbon is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Graphite.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Graphite has a layered structure composed of stacked sheets of six carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal crystal structure**.

 
 
• **It is the most stable form of pure carbon under standard conditions**.
 
• It is **very soft** with **low specific gravity** and **high electrical and thermal conductivity**.
 
• Naturally, high temperature and pressure change carbon into graphite.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/74e333d3c63b85c859dc15ee4a69582a90d13e711448cbfe9900cc4094065f6e.png] **__

 
• **Uses**:

 
 
• As neutron moderator in certain nuclear reactors,
 
• In pencil lead
 
• As Electrodes in batteries,
 
• As brake linings for heavy vehicles.
 
• Brushes of a DC motor

questions.question: In fireworks which metal is used for yellow colour?
questions.solution:
**__Explanation:__**

 
• Metal salts commonly used in** firework displays **include calcium chloride, sodium nitrate, barium chloride, copper chloride, etc.
 
• The green flame produced in fireworks is due to the presence of Barium.
 
• The blue flame is due to the presence of Copper.
 
• The orange flame is due to the presence of Calcium.
 
• A yellow flame is due to the presence of Sodium.
 
• Lithium /**Strontium** are used to impart a red colour to fireworks.

So, **Sodium** metal is used for yellow colour In fireworks.

questions.question: Which of the following is a thermosetting plastic?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bakelite**__.

__
 
• **Bakelite is a thermosetting plastic.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thermosetting plastics: **

 
 
• These are the polymers which when condensed have** a permanent change on heating.**
 
• On heating they undergo extensive cross-linking in molds and become hard and infusible; therefore, they cannot be reused.
 
• Its examples are **Bakelite, glyptal.**
 
 
 
• **Bakelite (Phenol-formaldehyde resin): **
 
 
• It is a** condensation polymer**.
 
• It is obtained from** phenol and formaldehyde** in presence of either an **acid or a base catalyst.**
 
• It is used in making** combs, fountain pens, photographs, records, electrical goods, etc**.​
 
• It was invented by **Leo H Baekeland**.
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Poly Vinyl Chloride(PVC) **is a synthetic plastic polymer.

 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/29109c1fe857b2d15f48d8a5298d6a27f298b4756c06b0e740da516df6a4ca85.png] 
 
 
 
• **Polyester **is a polymer of the **ester functional group**.
 
• There are two kinds of polyesters that each lead to thermoplastic or thermosetting products. The difference between the two kinds of polyester is their chemical structures.
